Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — saggiamente.com serves sponsored Mac-app banner cards (the reporter's ML BENCHMARK card plus MacAnvil/Octobar creatives) from its own banner plugin as the fallback fill of its ad slots when the Google Ad Manager ad is blocked. The domain-scoped rule saggiamente.com#⁠#⁠.sm-banner__nostro hides all four such slots with intact page layout, but the vision review keeps counting the site's own SaggeOfferte affiliate-offers widget and a lazy-loaded article image as unresolved ad instances, so the verified-in-DOM candidate is carried for human review instead of proposed.

## Candidate for review

`saggiamente.com##.sm-banner__nostro`

ItalianFilter/sections/specific.txt

Not verified: environmentExperiment returned inconclusive with failedCandidateChecks empty, and the bound visualReview returned verdict 'rejected' with symptom 'not_resolved' only because its remainingInstances are (1) the site's own SaggeOfferte affiliate-offers widget div.saggeofferte-widget, whose links all point to the owner's own network site saggeofferte.it, and (2) a \~450 px 'reserved gap' that DOM checks proved is the article's own <⁠p⁠><⁠img class="aligncenter size-full wp-image-132590" src=".../IMG_3838.jpeg"⁠> figure left blank by lazy loading. The targeted .sm-banner__nostro creatives (the reporter's ML BENCHMARK card among them) were confirmed hidden, pageIntegrity was intact, observedDamage empty, and #⁠adv_home_sidebar_top collapsed from 250 px to 0. Removing the remaining affiliate widget would mean deliberately hiding the site owner's own self-promotion, which the run instruction's filter policy forbids.

## Still visible after the rule

- Right sidebar top — SAGGOFFERTE / Tutte le offerte — Large rounded promotional/affiliate offers card in the right sidebar, with the SAGGOFFERTE heading, product offer rows, IL MIGLIORE badges, and an affiliate-commission disclosure. It occupies the top sidebar promotional slot.
- Una svolta importante, ma tutta da valutare — Large reserved blank gap (roughly 450–500 px tall, far larger than the normal paragraph/section spacing seen elsewhere) between the end of the pricing discussion and the next section heading — a leftover empty ad slot region consistent with the reporter's advertising symptom footprint. No creative, label or frame is visible in it.
- Right sidebar, top ad slot (below the page header, roughly y 215–820):⁠ rounded bordered card headed 'SAGGOFFERTE' with 'Tutte le offerte →' link, containing five sponsored affiliate product cards (Apple Watch Ultra 3 ×2, Marshall Monitor III ANC, DJI Osmo Pocket 4P Combo ×2) each with prices, discount badges and 'IL MIGLIORE' labels, footnoted 'OTTENIAMO COMMISSIONI DALLE VENDITE CON LINK AFFILIATI' — Sponsored promotional card occupying the sidebar advertising slot — the same position as the reporter's ML BENCHMARK ad card. Visible commercial/affiliate promo block that repeats the reporter-described symptom of ad cards shown on the article page.

## Executor and version

Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3

## Missing information

- Run instruction does not define "the site's own advertising (first-party ads)": The instruction's filter policy closes reports for "The site's own advertising (first-party ads)" with no rule, but neither the instruction nor the served policy/contributing documents define whether that means (a) self-promotion of goods/services owned by the site owner, or (b) any advertising served from the site's own domain regardless of who pays. On saggiamente.com both readings are plausible:⁠ the reported cards are sponsored creatives for third-party Mac apps (rel="sponsored") served by the site's own banner plugin from its own uploads and shown as the fallback fill when the site's Google Ad Manager slot is blocked, while a separate SaggeOfferte affiliate-offers widget on the same page links only to the owner's own network site. I resolved it from the KnowledgeBase terminology (self-promotion = goods/services owned by the site owner with no third-party compensation) and from the ad-blocking-filters purpose list ("Anti-adblock advertising — alternative advertising displayed on the site when the main one is blocked"), but an explicit definition in the run instruction would remove the ambiguity.

The reported defect was not reproduced

## Reproduced symptom

Not reproduced — With the reporter's own filter set and stealth settings loaded, the reported checkout card section renders normally (real card number / expiry / CVC fields with brand icons) on two independent loads, and the unfiltered control session looks the same, so the reported incorrect blocking does not reproduce. No repository rule hides or blocks the checkout — only captcha/anti-bot allow-exceptions and a decoy-element CSS rule were applied and only tracking beacons were blocked — so no rule is needed; recommend closing for a maintainer to confirm.

## Executor and version

Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3

## Policy rationale

No repository policy rule closes this report:⁠ it is not a first-party ad, not a paywall, not a German anti-adblock wall, and there is no anti-adblock wall on the page at all, so rule generation was permitted and the conclusion rests on live evidence rather than policy. The AdGuard filter policy guidance served for this run states that tracking-protection filters must not block a tracker when that disrupts site function (anti-bot/fraud protection such as PerimeterX or hCaptcha), which is why no candidate that would block the checkout's anti-bot or card-element hosts is appropriate.

Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — The reported defect is the Real Cookie Banner (RCB 5.1.6) consent overlay 'Privatsphäre-Einstellungen' that covers and blurs the weingut-bienert.de homepage on load; the fix is weingut-bienert.de#⁠$?#⁠div[⁠consent-skip-blocker]⁠ { remove:⁠ true; }, the domain-scoped form of the existing shared rule in the AdGuard Cookie Notices filter, verified by the A/B/C experiment with the symptom resolved and page integrity intact. ## Rule `weingut-bienert.de#$?#div[consent-skip-blocker] { remove: true; }` ## Policy rationale The run instruction's closing rules do not apply:⁠ this is not the site's own advertising, not a paywall, and the page shows a cookie-consent dialog rather than a German anti-adblock wall (no ad-block detection is involved; the reporter's 'Annoyance'/'Cookie' framing matches what the page itself shows). The filter policy makes the AdGuard Cookie Notices filter responsible for cookie notices and CMP requests and states that hiding or blocking the corresponding markup or scripts is usually sufficient, so a rule is in scope. Maintainer rules favour extending an existing shared rule over writing a new one:⁠ the reported domain is missing from the established multi-domain rule for this Real Cookie Banner markup, so the fix is submitted as the domain-scoped form of that rule for the host to merge into the shared domain list. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/f0e1dfd27e1622cc6069c5a332c6ab17ea0c4628/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) By adding the domain to the existing rule on [line 365](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/f0e1dfd27e1622cc6069c5a332c6ab17ea0c4628/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt#L365). ## Screenshots

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — notability.com/pricing shows a fixed Ketch cookie-consent sheet (#⁠ketch-consent-banner) covering the plan content; the repository already hides exactly that element on six other Ketch sites, so the fix adds notability.com to that shared rule, and the A/B experiment verified the reported sheet disappears with the page left intact. ## Rule `notability.com###ketch-consent-banner` ## Policy rationale The report is a cookie-notice annoyance, not first-party advertising, a paywall, a German anti-adblock wall or a scam page, so no policy rule closes it. The AdGuard Cookie Notices filter exists to block cookie notices and CMP requests, so the rule belongs in this repository's annoyance filters. The fix extends an existing shared multi-domain rule for the same CMP (the #⁠#⁠#⁠ketch-consent-banner family), as the maintainer rules require; that rule is not grouped for a single project. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/f0e1dfd27e1622cc6069c5a332c6ab17ea0c4628/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) By adding the domain to the existing rule on [line 3178](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/f0e1dfd27e1622cc6069c5a332c6ab17ea0c4628/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt#L3178). ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |
## Artifacts https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/40787282808 Automated analysis against filters at `f0e1dfd`. Posted by a filters agent; a maintainer reviews before anything is merged.
